WhatItMeans: Someone who is proud and full of themselves is heading for a humiliating fall — arrogance always comes before the crash.
WhatTheBibleSays: The warning is thoroughly biblical: Proverbs 11:2 says when pride cometh, then cometh shame, Proverbs 18:12 says before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and James 4:6 says God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble. The problem is only the wording — Proverbs 16:18 in the KJV reads 'Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall,' so the popular saying stitches half of each clause together and drops 'destruction' altogether. I believe the saying is true, and my position is that it belongs on the borderline: close enough to the verse that a reader could fairly call it the verse in other words, yet not the verse itself.
Origin: It is a popular paraphrase of Proverbs 16:18, shortened over time until the two halves of the verse were folded into one line. No separate author or date stands behind it; it grew out of the verse itself as people repeated it from memory.
Sources: Proverbial paraphrase of Proverbs 16:18; on-site KJV text
